reasons: No test or other evidence is visible.
The empty case is handled with a clear message.

terms.meaning: A reusable piece of logic that holds state inside a component.
A total or summary built from many separate values.
The address of one stored value inside a project record, used to find its evidence.
A panel that slides in over the page.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header comment on purpose
sections.what: A comment block explaining that summary figures are built from project datapoints, and that the panel lists them with their citations.
sections.why: Written to explain intent. No code runs here.
sections.watch_out: Keep the comment accurate if the panel's behavior changes.

sections.name: Datapoint, PanelState
sections.title: Datapoint shape and panel state
sections.what: Defines one datapoint: project id and name, label, displayed value, the field path that backs it, and an optional link. Also defines the internal panel state with title, optional note and item list.
sections.why: Gives every caller one fixed shape so the panel knows what to show.
sections.watch_out: A datapoint with no field path cannot open a citation, so the caller must supply it.

sections.name: useDatapointSources (part 1)
sections.title: Opening the panel and grouping items
sections.what: Stores the panel contents, open flag and display limit. openDatapoints fills in the title, items and note, resets the limit and opens the panel. Items are grouped by project up to the current limit, and the project count is worked out.
sections.why: Likely reason: the limit keeps a figure with many datapoints from drawing too many rows at once.
sections.watch_out: Grouping uses only the items up to the limit, while the header counts all items.

sections.name: useDatapointSources (part 2)
sections.title: Panel contents and citation click
sections.what: Builds the drawer: a heading, a count sentence, an optional note, an empty message, each project with an optional Project page link, each value as a clickable button that opens its full citation, and a Show more button when items remain. Includes the shared citation drawer.
sections.why: Each value opens its own source so the reader can check the number, which is the purpose of the panel.
sections.watch_out: Row keys use label plus field path, so two rows with the same pair can clash.

sections.name: SourcesButton
sections.title: Sources trigger button
sections.what: A small underlined Sources button in a monospace font. A figure heading uses it to open the panel. The caller passes its label and test id.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the purpose in the header comment.
sections.watch_out: Each test id must be unique, or automated tests may click the wrong button.

summary: A helper that lists each project value behind a total or chart point, and lets the reader open the source citation for each value.
purpose: When a reader clicks Sources on a summary figure, this shows the individual datapoints that make it up, grouped by project.
why: The header comment says summary figures are built from per-project datapoints, so the panel lets readers check where each figure comes from.
how: The hook holds the panel contents and open state. openDatapoints receives a title, a list of datapoints and an optional note, then opens the panel. The panel groups datapoints by project and shows up to a limit that starts at 100. Show more reveals 200 more at a time. Clicking a value opens the shared citation drawer for that project field. A Project page link closes the panel and navigates. SourcesButton is the small trigger shown on figures.
inputs: From the calling screen: a title, a list of datapoints (project id and name, label, displayed value, field path and an optional link), and an optional note.
outputs: A drawer panel with grouped datapoints, and the citation drawer when a value is clicked. SourcesButton draws a small underlined button.
risks: Only the first items up to the limit are grouped, but the count sentence uses all items, so the two can disagree until Show more is clicked. Row keys use label plus field path, which can repeat. Each Sources button needs a unique test id.
debug: If the panel is empty, check that the calling screen passed datapoints. If a click shows the wrong source, check the field path for that datapoint. If the count looks wrong, check the limit and the Show more button.
